subject: Private deployment commercial proposal and support-credit request
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Private deployment commercial proposal and next steps

Hi Elena / Oliver,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is our updated private deployment commercial proposal (v3) and an initial SOW draft for the on-prem/VPC deployment. High-level notes:

- Two licensing models included: per-node perpetual license + annual platform fee, or subscription (monthly) covering both license + platform fee.
- Platform fee options include a standard rate and a reduced regional bundle if you commit 12 months and cross-region support (EU + UK) is selected.
- Support tiers in the spreadsheet show Standard, Premium, and Enterprise (24/7 + named TAM). We included examples of migration credits for the first 60 days.

Questions for you: do you have a preference between per-node licensing vs subscription? Any procurement constraints around upfront platform fees vs amortized billing?

I’ve copied Ben and Marissa from Sales/CS so we can align on rollout and credits. If this looks reasonable, I can prepare a DocuSign for the commercial term sheet and lock in pricing for 30 days.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0198

Attachments: Redwood_Private_Pricing_Proposal_v3.pdf, SOW-Acme-Draft.docx, support-tiers-comparison.xlsx

From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@acmecorp.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T10:03:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment commercial proposal and next steps

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the proposal and attachments — this is helpful. A few procurement / finance items that will determine next steps on our side:

- Platform fee profile: our CFO prefers amortizing larger platform fees across the year rather than big upfront payments. Can you show a 12-month amortized option with clear monthly line items for tax/accounting?
- Discount ask: to get internal approval we need a better uplift on the first-year platform fee and support — our goal is to reduce TCO in year one by ~25% vs the baseline in v3.
- Migration credits: how many hours/credits do you typically offer for a zero-downtime migration? We need a concrete number to model professional services costs.
- SOW items: we’ll need clear acceptance criteria and an explicit rollback plan in the SOW (our legal/security team requires this).

Can Ben or Marissa run the amortized pricing scenarios and candidate concessions? If we can get a 12-month amortized invoice schedule and an initial discount tied to a 12-month commitment, we can move quickly.

Best,
Elena Martinez
Head of Cloud Procurement | Acme Corp
elena.martinez@acmecorp.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-23T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment commercial proposal and next steps

Elena — thanks for the clear feedback. Couple of proposals we can make to bridge to approval: 

1) Amortized invoice schedule: we’ll produce a 12-month amortized schedule for the platform fee (monthly line items) as requested. That will keep your finance team happy while letting us reserve capacity.

2) First-year commercial concession: if Acme commits to 12 months and signs by Apr 30, we can offer a 18% reduction to the platform fee for year one (applies to either licensing model).

3) Migration credits & PS: we can include 240 hours of migration engineering credits (applies to go-live work and early optimization). Any additional PS work would be scoped at a reduced day rate tied to the committed term.

4) Support tier: we can provide a 20% discount on Premium support for the first 12 months and include one named TAM onboarding call per month during the initial 90 days. Enterprise SLA add-ons are available as optional line items.

5) SOW: we’ll add explicit acceptance criteria and a rollback plan to the SOW draft. We’ll flag the security artifacts (SOC2/ISO) and propose a targeted handover to our Security PM to satisfy your team.

If these concessions are acceptable, we’ll update the commercial spreadsheet and push a DocuSign term sheet. For timing: Ben/Marissa will run numbers and share the amortized invoice schedule by Tue (Mar 24).

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1-650-555-0123

From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@acmecorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-03-25T11:18:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment commercial proposal and next steps

Ben / Sofia — appreciate the fast turnaround and the concessions. A few points before we proceed to signature: 

- The 18% platform fee reduction is a good start, but our finance team is pushing for a 22% reduction in year one to hit internal targets. Can you split the difference and agree to 20% if we extend the acceptance window from 30 to 60 days?
- Migration credits: 240 hours is reasonable, but we’d like to convert up to 80 of those hours into fixed deliverables (runbook, automated rollback scripts) so they’re guaranteed.
- SOW: legal wants a 60-day acceptance window post-go-live and a clearly defined business continuity clause. We can accept the rollback plan language if it includes explicit RTO/RPO figures.

Quoted for reference:
> On Mon, Mar 23, 2026 at 14:27 Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> > If Acme commits to 12 months and signs by Apr 30, we can offer a 18% reduction to the platform fee for year one
>
We can do 20% if there’s an extended acceptance window and conversion of migration hours into defined deliverables. Please confirm and we’ll route to procurement for final review.

Regards,
Elena
Elena Martinez
Head of Cloud Procurement | Acme Corp

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-27T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment commercial proposal and next steps — proposed final commercial terms

Elena / Oliver — thanks, and good negotiation. Summarizing the commercial terms we can commit to for the Term Sheet and DocuSign: 

- Platform fee: 20% off the v3 baseline for year one (applies to either Per-node license + annual platform fee or Subscription model).
- Acceptance window: extended to 60 days post-go-live as requested; SOW will include RTO/RPO figures and a rollback plan.
- Migration credits: 240 hours total; up to 80 hours converted to fixed deliverables (runbook, automated rollback scripts, one knowledge-transfer workshop).
- Support: 20% discount on Premium support for first 12 months; monthly TAM onboarding calls for first 90 days included.
- Billing: we’ll provide a 12-month amortized invoice schedule for the platform fee to meet your finance requirements.

Next steps: Ben and Marissa will update the pricing spreadsheet and SOW. I will prepare the DocuSign term sheet with the above concessions and route it to your signature with a 60-day hold for acceptance. We’ll also attach the security evidence pack (SOC2) in the next email for your security reviewers.

If that matches your expectations, please reply with an approval-to-proceed and we’ll push the updated docs. Targeting commercial sign by Apr 30 to lock the committed credits/pricing.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
